text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria's president-elect Petar Stoyanov said he would ask the ruling Socialist party to form a new government if outgoing president Zhelyu Zhelev has not done so by the end of his term of office on January 22.
-- Bulgaria's opposition said it was ready to begin talks with the ruling Socialists on a national anti-crisis programme. @
-- Bulgaria's State Railways (BSR) has proposed to the outgoing cabinet to raise railway passenger fares by 39 percent from February 1, a BSR top official said.

-- Bulgaria's state monopolist cigarette maker Bulgartabak holdind is expected to ask the outgoing cabinet to raise prices of locally made cigarettes by 25 percent from February 1, a Bulgartabak official said.

-- Bulgaria expected to finalise the sale of 25 percent of the Bulgarian Telecommunication Company by July-August and possible payments could be expected by the year's end, outgoing deputy prime minister Roumen Gechev said. @
-- Bulgaria's ruling Socialist party said its deputies will attend parliament on Sunday when president-elect Peter Stoyanov is due to be sworn in, party leader Georgi Parvanov said.

-- Direct foreign investments in Bulgaria totalled $262.5 million by December 10, and the total amount for last year was expected at around $280 million, Foreign Investment Agency preliminary figures showed.
-- Food prices rose 30.8 percent from December 28 to January 15, National Statistics Institute preliminary figures showed.
-- Bulgaria's domestic debt rose by 214 billion levs in December to 1,052 trillion levs, Finance ministry figures showed. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
